title: Introduce slot-orchestra allocator and lane-based compactor to tame KV cache fragmentation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Our GPU KV cache shows sustained internal fragmentation across diverse serving workloads (short-chat bursts, long-completion generation, multi-turn chat). Fragmentation causes: many small-lived entries from chat-type requests, large long-lived KV pages from long-completions, and allocation churn amplified by continuous batching and model shard placement. Symptoms include elevated GPU memory use for the same token set, increased compaction CPU spikes, and occasional headroom loss under load. This ticket proposes a new allocation strategy (slot-orchestra) plus a lane-based background compactor to reduce fragmentation while preserving low tail latency for continuous batching.
background: Current allocator is a general slab/pool hybrid tuned for throughput. It minimizes per-allocation overhead but treats all entries uniformly, which creates cross-workload interference: short-lived tokens and long-lived KV pages are co-located and cause holes that are expensive to coalesce on GPUs. Continuous batching increases concurrent allocation pressure (many prefix caches live simultaneously) and widens allocation size distribution. Prior work focused on defragmentation passes and soft-reserve windows but did not partition allocations by workload heat or lifecycle characteristics.
proposed_solution: 1) Slot-Orchestra allocator: partition KV cache into logical lanes (hot,warm,cold,ephemeral) and assign mini-pools (micro-slabs) per lane and per model-shard. Allocation heuristics place new entries into a lane based on observed token access frequency and expected TTL from serving metadata (e.g., short-chat indicator, generation context length). 2) Lane-based compactor: a background, rate-limited compaction thread per lane that performs compaction within a lane first (cheap, high ROI) and cross-lane migration for persistent imbalances. 3) Micro-slab fast-path: very small KV entries (<128B) are serviced from a packed micro-slab to avoid inflating larger slab fragmentation. 4) Batch-aware eviction hints: continuous batching runtime emits eviction hints at batch boundaries, allowing the allocator to perform batch-aligned migrations that avoid hot stalls during kernel launches. 5) Controlled compaction windows: compaction jobs are scheduled during soft-idle windows detected by the batch scheduler and throttled by a global compaction budget to protect p95 latency. 6) Telemetry and canary toggle: add metrics to measure fragmentation ratio, compaction CPU/time, allocation churn by lane, and expose kv_allocator=v2 toggle for gradual rollout.
tradeoffs: - Complexity: introduces per-lane logic and a compaction scheduler; increases code surface area and maintenance burden. - Edge cases: misclassification of entries can move frequently-accessed items into cold lanes; to mitigate we add a migration hotness detector and aging counters. - Memory overhead: per-lane mini-pools may create temporary buffer headroom; we target <2% additional reserved headroom overall. - Performance risk: compaction must not regress p95; we limit compaction concurrency and schedule during low-batch pressure.
tasks: Write design doc and diagrams (Confluence) explaining lane heuristics and compaction flow
Prototype Slot-Orchestra allocator in runtime branch (C++)
Integrate allocation hints into continuous-batching runtime
Implement lane-based compaction thread with global rate limiter
Add telemetry (fragmentation_ratio, lane_allocation_counts, compaction_time_ms, move_rate) and Grafana dashboards
Create synthetic benchmarks: short-chat, long-generation, mixed traffic; measure fragmentation and memory headroom
Integrate unit and e2e tests; add canary toggle (kv_allocator=v2) and rollback path
Code review and performance sign-off; prepare rollout playbook and runbook
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio (wasted_alloc_bytes / total_alloc_bytes) reduced by >=40% on mixed traffic benchmark
Average GPU memory headroom improved by >=6% for production-like workloads
No regression in p95 token latency >5% compared to baseline during canary
Compaction CPU cost stays <7% of serving CPU across steady-state workloads
Telemetry coverage: lane allocation counts, per-lane fragmentation, compaction_time_ms, move_rate, compaction_backpressure_signals are all emitted and dashboarded
Rollback toggle correctly disables allocator and returns to previous state without leaks
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit and bench validation in dev cluster. Stage 1: internal staging cluster with shadow traffic and telemetry validation. Stage 2: Canary on 5% of hosted pool for 72 hours; monitor dashboards and automated alerts for p95 regressions and OOMs. Stage 3: Ramp to 25% and run full mixed-workload soak for 72 hours. Stage 4: 50% ramp and then full rollout if metrics stable. Provide immediate rollback via kv_allocator=v1 toggle and circuit-breaker to disable compaction threads. Post-rollout retro and playbook update.
notes_updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting; agreed on lane taxonomy (hot/warm/cold/ephemeral) and micro-slab threshold of 128B.
2025-01-15: Design review - Linnea Bergstrom requested clearer migration heuristics; added aging counters and hotness detector to proposed_solution.
2025-01-22: Prototype allocator scaffolding merged to feature branch; basic micro-slab allocator passes unit tests.
2025-01-28: First lab benchmark: mixed workload shows 25% fragmentation reduction vs baseline; compaction CPU at ~3%. Need to improve long-lived page handling.
2025-02-02: Implemented batch-aligned eviction hints; local bench shows improved migration latency during compaction windows.
2025-02-05: Preparing staging canary artifacts and dashboards; PR referenced in links is open for review.
